_comment: Mutation testing for the kernel's load-bearing maths.
Coverage answers 'was this line run', which is the wrong question. The July audit found 86
real defects behind a green suite at 88% coverage — that gap IS the signature of
coverage-measured testing. Mutation testing asks the right question: if this line were
wrong, would anything fail? The kill rate is the only objective number this repository has
for the strength of its assertions, and it is the honest way to re-derive the lost
medium/low backlog rather than re-guess it.
Scoped to store/, crs/, layers/ and commands/ on purpose. They are where a silent wrong
answer becomes a wrong number on a deed, they are pure enough to mutate meaningfully, and
starting narrow keeps a full run in minutes rather than an hour. Widen it once these are
clean. Renderers are excluded: their real behaviour is MapLibre's, which lives in the
browser suite.
Thresholds are a ratchet, not an aspiration. `break` sits at the current measured floor so
the number can only go up; raise it when a run beats it.
BASELINE, 2026-08-18, first full run: 65.50% overall. The distribution was the finding, not
the average — SpatialIndex.ts sat at 34.62%, the worst file in the repo, on the R-tree
behind query() and nearest(). FeatureStore.ts 54.50%, builtins.ts 61.54%, CrsService.ts
63.29%. Against ~89% line coverage, and that gap between covered and killed is precisely
the shape the July audit left behind: 86 real defects behind a green suite.
2026-08-24, after SpatialIndex.test.ts: 66.70% overall — 1249 killed, 17 timed out, 537
survived, 95 with no coverage at all, over 1898 mutants. `break` raised 65 -> 66.
SpatialIndex.ts     96.15%   was 34.62% — see below
FeatureStore.ts     54.89%   still the weakest, and now the obvious next target
builtins.ts         61.78%   CrsService.ts 64.63%   rasterLayerType.ts 66.18%
vectorLayerType.ts  70.59%   CommandBus.ts 72.58%   planar.ts 74.31%
LayerManager.ts     74.56%   TopologyIndex.ts 75.96%   registry.ts 80.77%
SpatialIndex went up because it had never been imported by a test — everything reached it
through BlaeuCollection, which looks each returned id up in the feature map and silently
drops the misses, so an index that over-reports still answers correctly. 25 of its 26
mutants are now killed and **96.15% is its ceiling, not a shortfall**: the survivor is
equivalent. With `if (false) return`, an unknown id falls through to rbush.remove(undefined),
which opens `if (!item) return this`, and to a Map.delete of an absent key — nothing
observable changes. Killing it would mean widening remove() to return a boolean, which is a
public API change made to move a metric. Do not.
Note the mutant count differs between the two runs — 1877 in the 2026-08-18 CI figure, 1898
measured locally on both 2026-08-24 runs. The cause was not chased; the point is that the
before/after comparison above is between two runs of the same 1898, so it is sound. Compare
scores across dates, not counts.
